root_idea.summary: The root is centered on splitting or slitting, with a related semantic development toward exceeding the proper limit in exultation.
root_idea.development: The concrete sense of cutting or dividing is associated with veterinary terminology, while بَطَرَ denotes excessive exultation that exceeds proper bounds, especially in response to prosperity.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed as the Quran-attested abstract noun بَطَر.

senses.definition: To be overwhelmed by prosperity or blessing and thereby rejoice or exult excessively, behaving insolently and ungratefully, or misusing what one has been given.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَهَا, the verb describes prosperity-driven exultation in a community's life. The construction is explained as intransitive, with مَعِيشَتَهَا in the accusative associated with an understood في.

senses.definition: Exultant insolence arising from poor tolerance of prosperity or blessing, with failure to fulfill its due or diversion of it to a wrong use.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression بَطَرًا وَرِئَاءَ النَّاسِ, the noun denotes boastful, prosperity-related exultation accompanying ostentation before people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In wealth- and favor-related constructions, to domineer over others when rich, or to hold wealth or a benefit lightly and be ungrateful for it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This includes constructions with الغنى and النعمة and describes a broader application of insolent behavior toward prosperity or favor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become confounded, perplexed, or amazed through fright.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct Classical use from prosperity-related exultation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To refuse right guidance in managing one's affairs, or to disdain and reject truth or duty as false or unacceptable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The constructions بَطِرَ هِدَايَةَ أَمْرِهِ and بَطَرُ الحَقِّ are used for refusal to recognize or accept right guidance and truth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To regard something with hatred or dislike despite its not deserving such treatment.
To be brisk, lively, or sprightly.
To walk with an elegant, proud, self-conceited gait, inclining the body from side to side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a conventional description of manner of walking, not a general restriction on the verb's objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or divide something lengthwise; to slit or split it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the transitive cutting branch of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to become exultant, insolent, and ungrateful, or to stupefy and confound him, turning him from moderation or gravity into levity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative may describe wealth producing this condition or another circumstance causing a person's composure to collapse into excessive exultation or confusion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impose on someone what exceeds his ability; alternatively, to cut off his means of subsistence and waste his body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In أَبْطَرَهُ ذَرْعَهُ, the expression is explained either as overtaxing someone beyond his power or as destroying his means and bodily condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To practice farriery or veterinary medicine; to treat beasts, including horses and similar animals, medically or curatively.
In the phrase ذَهَبَ دَمُهُ بِطْرًا, to go unavenged because the blood has been held in light estimation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic use concerning blood or a blood-debt that is disregarded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Exulting greatly or excessively and behaving insolently and ungratefully, especially through pride in wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the active-participial adjective of بَطِرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cut or divided lengthwise; slit or split.
A feminine adjective for one who behaves with much exultation, insolence, and unthankfulness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form is grammatical; the lexical description concerns the behavior, not a restriction to a particular class of person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clamorous or long-tongued; one who persists in error; also, one who behaves with exultant insolence and ingratitude.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence records frequent application of this adjective in reference to women, but that usage distribution is not a semantic restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tailor, in an extension associated with cutting or slitting.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the verbal-noun name of the veterinary practice denoted by بَيْطَرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A farrier or veterinarian who treats beasts medically; figuratively, a person highly knowledgeable or skilful in a matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative use extends the expertise of a veterinary practitioner to skill in another field.
